chunks: A number of our companions, from our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abdul A'la ibn Ayn, the slave of the progeny of Saam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Marry the virgins, for they are the finest of the mouths.'
And in another Hadith, he said: 'And the toughest of the wombs, and the roundest of the behinds, and the most open of the wombs (for childbirth).'
'Do you not know that I would be priding with you (among) the communities on the Day of Judgement, even with the miscarried child remaining at the Door of the Paradise.'
'So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would be Saying: “Enter the Paradise!” So it would be saying, “I shall not enter until my parents enter before me.”'
'So Allah, Blessed and High, would be Saying to an Angel from the Angels: “Come to Me with its parents.” So He would be Commanding with both of them to the Paradise.'
'And He would be Saying: “This is by the Grace of My Mercy to you.”'

key_terms.أَفْوَاهاً: Finest or most pleasant in speech/mouths
key_terms.الْأَبْكَارَ: The virgins (females who have not been married or had intercourse)
key_terms.مُحْبَنْطِئاً: Waiting or lingering (specifically at the gate)

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues of marrying virgins and the status of the miscarried child in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Prophetic preference for virgins (bakar) based on their physical ease in childbirth and emotional freshness, a view supported by Shia jurists regarding marital compatibility. It further illustrates the concept of divine mercy extending to the 'saght' (miscarried fetus), who acts as an intercessor for his parents' entry into Paradise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual status of the unborn.
